issues.description: `import sys` is missing in numba/cpython/mathimpl.py and numba/np/math/mathimpl.py
issues.detail: Both files reference `sys.version_info` in new guards but neither diff adds `import sys`. If `sys` is not already imported at module top, import time will raise `NameError` on Python 3.11+, breaking numba itself. The invariant `sys is defined before use` must be audited and satisfied before merge.

issues.description: Version guard placed inside class body breaks `Math_unary` registration indentation
issues.detail: In `mathdecl.py`, the new `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` block sits at module scope but immediately follows the `Math_unary` class body with a removed blank line. The control flow is correct but readability is degraded; a careful reader cannot tell at a glance whether the guard belongs to the class. Add a blank line and a one-line comment stating the invariant: `math.exp2` exists only on CPython >= 3.11.

issues.description: Test `x_values` includes negative inputs for unsigned types, silently wrapping
issues.detail: `x_values = [-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]` is reused verbatim from `test_exp`, but `run_unary` pairs these against `uint16/uint32/uint64`. Negative ints will be coerced (wrap or error depending on path), so the test is not actually exercising `exp2` on the stated domain. State the invariant per type or split the value list; otherwise the test's coverage claim is asymptotically-OK-practically-wrong.

issues.description: Release note file missing trailing newline
issues.detail: `docs/upcoming_changes/10276.new_feature.rst` ends with `No newline at end of file`. POSIX text files should terminate with `\n`; some RST toolchains and linters flag this. Trivial fix, but worth doing for a file that exists to be read.

issues.description: No literate comment explaining why the 3.11 guard exists
issues.detail: Three sites now carry `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` with no comment. The reader must know that `math.exp2` was added in CPython 3.11 to understand why these guards exist and why omitting the guard would `AttributeError` at import. One-line comment at each site (or a shared constant `_HAS_MATH_EXP2`) would make the code readable without running it.

issues.description: Duplicate guard across three files invites drift; consider a single capability flag
issues.detail: The same `sys.version_info >= (3, 11)` predicate is repeated in `mathdecl.py`, `cpython/mathimpl.py`, and `np/math/mathimpl.py`. A single `_HAS_MATH_EXP2 = sys.version_info >= (3, 11)` in `numba.core.utils` (next to `PYVERSION`, which the test already imports) would centralize the invariant and prevent partial-support drift if 3.10 is dropped later.

review.summary: The change is small and the algorithmic content is trivial — `math.exp2` maps to the `llvm.exp2` intrinsic via the existing `unary_math_intr` machinery, which is the right data-structure-level reuse. The rigor gap is in the version guard: `sys` is referenced in two `mathimpl.py` files where the diff does not show an `import sys`, which must be verified before merge or import will fail on 3.11+. The test reuses an x_values list that includes negatives against unsigned types, weakening the coverage claim. Overall: UNDER-AUDITED and NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT — correct in spirit, but the guard's invariant ("math.exp2 added in CPython 3.11") is nowhere stated and is duplicated three times.
